subject: Runtime Surge — Customer Situation Report & Commitment Timeline
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nimbushealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: ProcureOps <procure.ops@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partial availability on inference endpoints for prod-us (impacting user flows)

Hi Vivek —

We started seeing elevated 5xxs and timeouts on our prod-us inference routes around 08:40 PDT. Errors are intermittent but affecting match-rate calculations for a subset of requests (roughly 12% of traffic). The latency spikes have caused downstream syncs to back up.

Can you confirm whether this is a platform-side issue or something in our tenancy? We have an upcoming demo on Thurs and need an ETA for restoration or mitigations.

Attachments: sample_error_trace.txt (snippet), request_ids.txt (10 ids)

—Alex
Head of Integrations, NimbusHealth
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Partial availability on inference endpoints for prod-us (impacting user flows)

Team — forwarding NimbusHealth. They report intermittent 5xxs/timeouts on prod-us affecting critical customer flow. High priority.

Immediate asks:
- Marcus: spin up a diagnostic bridge (voice optional) and collect autoscaler & runtime logs for their tenant and the host cluster.
- Laura: pull routing and fallback policy history for prod-us; did any model variants or fallbacks trigger?
- Soojin: surface recent deploys, kernel changes, or infra config pushes in the last 6 hours.

I’ll reply to Alex with an acknowledgement and set expectation: we’ll provide an initial summary within 30 minutes and a mitigation ETA in 90 minutes. If you need bandwidth I can pull in ops.

—Vivek
Senior Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Partial availability on inference endpoints for prod-us (impacting user flows)

Setting up a bridge now (zoom + PST conf) — join code: RW-INC-6721.
Initial findings:
- Autoscaler oscillated between 6 -> 3 -> 7 pods over 08:30–09:10 with a short burst of OOM kills on one node at 08:48.
- Runtime logs show a small window of KV cache mis-indexing messages followed by retry storms from the customer SDK (their sample ids).
- No platform-wide deploys in prod-us in the last 12 hours; small runtime kernel selection change was deployed to a canary pool (not the prod pool).

Immediate mitigations in progress:
1) Pin NimbusHealth traffic to alternate pool with conservative batching parameters (reduces retry amplification).
2) Patch live autoscaler policy to floor to 4 pods while we stabilize.
3) Collect and attach runtime logs + host metrics (will push to the Drive link).

I’ll update in the bridge and then we can draft a customer note.

Attachments: runtime_logs_snippet.txt

—Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <procure.ops@nimbushealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Partial availability on inference endpoints for prod-us (impacting user flows)

Alex — quick update from our response war room: we’ve identified a localized runtime resource oscillation in prod-us that amplified when your SDK retried a subset of requests. Steps taken in the last 30 mins:

- Routed NimbusHealth traffic to an alternate serving pool to isolate impact.
- Increased autoscaler minimum to 4 for your tenancy to prevent under-provisioning while we investigate.
- Applied conservative batching overrides for your routes to reduce request amplification.

What this means for you now: error rates should materially drop within the next 10–15 minutes; full normalization within 60–90 minutes as caches warm and autoscaling stabilizes. We will monitor with you and share logs and a concrete timeline for root cause no later than 90 minutes from now.

Attachments: nimbus_incident_mitigation_plan_v2.pdf (short plan)

Requested from you: any additional request ids or SDK versions you can share will help us validate the mitigation.

We’ll follow up with a customer-facing summary and follow those with a post-incident timeline and action items.

—Vivek
Senior Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nimbushealth.com>

Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime Surge — Customer Situation Report & Commitment Timeline

Thanks Vivek — I can confirm error rates dropped substantially after 10:20. We still see a handful of timeouts (~1%) but nothing blocking the demo prep. Appreciate the rapid isolation.

Two asks for the postmortem:
1) Please include a simple timeline we can share with our security/compliance team.
2) Confirm whether the KV cache mis-indexing is user-impacting or a side-effect of the autoscaler oscillation.

I’ll attach our SDK version matrix and a couple more request ids in a follow-up thread.

—Alex
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Summary & next steps — incident INF-6721 (runtime surge, prod-us)

Alex — thank you again for the quick collaboration. Below is our executive-style summary and committed next steps for NimbusHealth. We will follow with a full post-incident report (PIR) in the next 48 hours.

Executive summary:
- Incident window: 2027-08-09T08:40:00-07:00 through 2027-08-09T10:00:00-07:00 (degraded but gradually remediated).
- Impact: intermittent 5xx and timeouts affecting ~12% of requests for NimbusHealth; upstream downstream sync delays for 30–45 minutes.
- Immediate cause: localized autoscaler oscillation coupled with client retry amplification; KV cache mis-indexing observed as a symptom during the spike.

Actions completed:
- Isolated customer traffic to alternate serving pool and adjusted batching/offload policy (completed 09:00 PDT).
- Raised autoscaler floor for Nimbus tenancy and applied guardrails (09:05 PDT).
- Disabled the canary kernel selector for pool 3 pending RCA (09:30 PDT).

Committed follow-ups (PIR deliverables):
1) Timeline with event markers and logs (48 hours).
2) Root-cause analysis of cache mis-index and autoscaler behavior; mitigation code changes or config hardening (7 days).
3) Customer-facing executive note suitable for compliance (48 hours).
4) Joint validation window with Nimbus SDK team to confirm no client-side amplification patterns (next 3 days, propose Wed 13 Aug 11:00 PDT).

Attachments: service-map.png, runtime_logs_snippet.txt

If this looks good I’ll convert into a short formal PIR and a one-page timeline you can share with your security team.

—Vivek
Senior Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
